intro: Oregon runs elections through its 36 county elections offices, with the Secretary of State's Elections Division overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Oregon votes by mail, so there is no ID check at a polling place. Sign your ballot return envelope. Your county checks the signature against your voter record. If it is missing or does not match, the county sends a notice, and you have until 21 days after the election to fix it.

elections.name: General election
elections.hours: All-mail election. Ballots are due by 8:00 pm, and county elections offices are open 7:00 am to 8:00 pm.
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any local measures. There are no statewide ballot measures this year. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: A new registrant must register by 11:59 pm Pacific time on the 21st day before the election.

dates.label: Ballots mailed to voters
dates.detail: Oregon mails a ballot to every active registered voter. This is the first day counties mail them. Voters whose status is inactive do not get a ballot.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Ballots are due by 8 pm. Return yours to an official drop box by 8 pm, or mail it with a postmark no later than Election Day.
